title: CVE-2026-31431: 'Copy Fail' lets one pod poison another on the same node
summary: A newly disclosed Kubernetes flaw lets an attacker sitting in one pod inject malicious code into binaries that other pods on the same node execute — with no elevated privileges, no container escape, and nothing left on the filesystem. If you pack untrusted workloads onto shared nodes, read this before your next scheduling decision.

title: TeamPCP turned your security tools into the attack
summary: Between late February and March 2026, the TeamPCP group ran an escalating supply-chain campaign that compromised widely trusted open-source security tooling — including the scanners Trivy and KICS and the LiteLLM AI gateway. The uncomfortable lesson: the tools you trust to find risk are themselves part of your attack surface.

title: When Trivy got weaponised: 75 of 76 tags poisoned
summary: In March 2026 attackers compromised the repository behind Trivy — one of the most widely used scanners in the Kubernetes world — force-pushed malicious binaries, and poisoned 75 of 76 version tags. Pinning by tag was not enough. Verify signatures and pin images by digest, not by a tag someone else can move.

title: Kubernetes token theft is up 282% — and IT is the target
summary: Unit 42 telemetry shows Kubernetes-focused attacker activity — including stealing service-account tokens — jumped 282% over the past year, with the IT sector absorbing the large majority of observed activity. Short-lived credentials and tight RBAC stopped being optional a while ago.

title: Securing AI workloads on Kubernetes after the LiteLLM breach
summary: The March 2026 LiteLLM supply-chain attack harvested LLM API keys, Kubernetes configs, and cloud credentials from every environment it reached. Pod Security Standards cover container hygiene — they say nothing about prompt injection, model integrity, or RAG retrieval abuse. AI on Kubernetes needs its own threat model.

title: 82% run Kubernetes in production — so the image is the front line
summary: The CNCF Annual Survey 2025 puts Kubernetes in production for 82% of container users. At that scale the container image supply chain becomes the primary attack vector — which is exactly why provenance, SBOMs, and admission policy keep climbing every team's roadmap.
